## Corrections as of 2026-08-15 — read before trusting anything below The dated entries below are kept as written; history is not edited here. These are the places the document is now known to be wrong or superseded. Full sweep: REVISION_REGISTER.md. 1. Law count — the 2026-08-13 entry says "box-and-box is 116 laws with 3 declared-open." It is 118 enforced (103 kernel + 15 compose/CC2) + 3 declared-open, re-derived 2026-08-15 by running both suites from a clean public clone. That entry was itself a correction (129 → 116) and it undercounted. The suites derive their totals — quote them, never hand-type the number. (The 2026-06-07 entry's "103 → 116" was true when written and stays.) 2. §3.1's Supabase route is abandoned (ruled 2026-07-30). studbook replaces it; spec rung, nothing migrated, ampersand-supabase archived-not-failed. The section already carries a note saying so; the schema inventory below it still reads as current architecture and is not. 3. §3.4's ten `live_deployed` Fly.io apps are being wound down. Ruled 2026-08-15: compute moves into the ComputeDriven OS, Cloudflare is the cloud side (R2 + Workers + D1), and Fly keeps exactly one thing — Keycloak, because Workers cannot run Java. §3.4 now carries the full note. The 2026-08-13 measurement stands; the plan around it is replaced. Nothing has been torn down, and nothing should be until its OS-side replacement is live_local. 4. §0/§6 ratings take Fly deployment state as an input, and item 3 changes that input. They are now stale rather than merely at risk — a wind-down is not a regression, but a rating that reads deployment breadth as strength will misread it as one. Not recomputed here: §0/§6 are a Travis rating exercise (the document already reserves the blended-vs-per-layer question for him), and the honest state is "input changed, not yet re-rated." 5. T&R backs up the user's machine, 10 GB–10 TB — not just the shell's graph. See WORLD_SIZE.md §11 for the measurement and the scope error it corrects.

Last updated: 2026-09-05 — Super R0b.R · R7–R13: the durable vocabulary for validation work, written one round BEFORE the first validation runs — and two pre-existing defects found by the act of writing it. In an isolated detached worktree at the exact R2–R6 tip 78b19e8 (super-r7, not pushed; the shared HEAD had moved under two site/-only commits and an evidence tree must not move beneath a semantic-schema slice). Two append-only ledger kinds, validation_job_started@1 / validation_job_outcome@1, and nothing mutates the first into the second — a start with no outcome is the honest representation of a Carrier that died mid-job, and strictly more informative than an INDETERMINATE invented to fill the row, which would be a claim made by a process that was not there about a moment nothing observed. So there is no INDETERMINATE. `state` and `verdict` are orthogonal and that is the whole design: a source-hygiene job that runs correctly and finds a NUL byte DID ITS WORK (completed · fail); one whose snapshot moved underneath it did not (failed · typed reason). A basis mismatch recorded as fail is a false statement about the source — it asserts a property of bytes nobody read — so both over-specifications are refused rather than stored with the extra field dropped. Six failure reasons, every one quoted to a line of code that can emit it (five format!s in host/src/effect.rs + lib.rs, one the runtime's own); GPT proposed scope-mismatch and carrier-failure and both were omitted because nothing can produce either yet and admitting them makes the enum a wish list. Three vocabularies kept apart: kind (row shape) ≠ validation_kind (the work) ≠ state/verdict (how it went). JobBasis (validation-job@1) lives in the worktree store beside `bases`, not its own — a job names sb_→wt_→rp_, one chain, and they must seal as one fact; it adds no authority store, so authority_stores/0, the seals report and the recovery manifest are unchanged. worker_generation is bound because Worker.reopen/1 advances it and still_standing/1 already refuses attachment-worker-generation-stale — derived from existing semantics, not added for safety-feel. Operator/host only, no `CommandSpec` entry: a check narrowing what an agent may name is not a reason to open a door, and whether an Actor may request a job against its own Worker's basis is named as open rather than answered. Validation.record_outcome/2 refuses unless inside the coordinator (unordered-validation-outcome) because every check it makes is a read-then-write of the ledger — a guarantee, not a habit.

The three defects the round found, all pre-existing, none introduced by it. Ampd.Worktree's :bind_basis was in @ordered_ops and not in @participant_mutations, so the participant boundary classified a write as a read: a lost reply to the one operation that mints source authority came back :unavailable (retryable, nothing mutated) when the truth is :indeterminate (a basis may be on disk; a human must look). Present since cbc9b99, the commit that introduced SourceBasis. And `tools/check-ordered-boundary.mjs` names that exact failure, was RED on it through all of Phase A and R2–R6, and nothing runs it — no verify, no release.sh, no battery; there was no runner for the static gates at all. A gate nobody invokes is not a gate, it is a file that would have caught something. tools/gates.sh is now that runner, with `CANNOT RUN` as a third verdict because a gate whose subject is unbuilt has measured nothing and scoring that as held or failed lies in one of two directions. Building it surfaced two more: both ordered gates hardcoded `const ROOT = '/home/travis/ProjectAmp2/super'`, so running them from a detached worktree measured the canonical tree — a green verdict about source the run never saw, in exactly the round that needed an isolated parent; and check-dispatch-partition.mjs shells to mix run and parses stdout, so a stale _build puts compiler output into the parse (a false 22 reads · 1 failed, deterministic 15 · 11 · 0 next run). Also fixed: ampd/priv/data/ had been **tracked since the repo's first commit despite the *.dets ignore rule — `.gitignore` is not consulted for a file git already tracks, so the rule protected every world except the ones a developer's runtime writes; the dogfood minted a live ledger into `receipts.dets` (5.9 → 18.8 KB) and committed it, plus an established worktree as a gitlink**. Untracked, ignored whole, and the runtime proven to boot from nothing rather than assumed to. And a third: Ampd.Projection says in its own docs that every window it hands out has a `next_cursor`, and every one of them needs a command that can follow it — a cursor with nothing to give it to is a promise the protocol does not keep — and R6 broke that rule the round it split `receipts` by kind, adding a worktree_receipts window with no door, in the very round whose finding was that an agent could not see the establishment of its own worktree. It could see it in the frame and could not page it; R7 would have done the same again with validations. Both commands now exist (list_worktree_receipts, list_validations — reads, :both channel, filter reused from history_for/2, no new authority), and the suite checks the rule rather than the two cases by walking every windowed key for a command. A gate caught the half of that which was got wrong: cockpit_test.exs derives its expected read list from CommandSpec.reads/0 and refused both as "declared in command-spec@1 and never exercised here".

Evidence (all serialized — config/config.exs points every checkout on this machine at the one fixed path /tmp/ampd-test-data and rm -rfs it at config load, so two suites running at once delete each other's world mid-run; measured as 30 failures of 54 in locus_test.exs with another suite running and 0 of 54 on the identical tree minutes later): super-host verify 319 held · 0 failed; ExUnit 673 / 0 against a 630 / 0 baseline at 78b19e8; multi-seed 0 · 424242 · 909090 all 666/0, retained with an orphan census per run; static gates 8 held · 0 failed · 0 could not run; scope-manifest vectors 12 held · 0 failed; tools/sabotage-validation.sh 25 caught · 0 NOT A FALSIFIER · 0 unapplied; isolated host sabotage 55 falsified · 0 did not · 0 could not ask on a 319/0 baseline, reproducing Phase A exactly. That last column is new because the harness's first version embedded Python in a shell string, the quoting did not survive, every stub silently failed to apply, the suites stayed green and eighteen cases were scored NOT A FALSIFIER — a harness that cannot tell "the mechanism was removed and nothing noticed" from "the mechanism was never removed" reports the wrong verdict with total confidence, which is the same defect it exists to find. Dogfooded end to end: tools/dogfood-validation.exs drives repository → Lane → Worker → worktree → SourceBasis → scope manifest → JobBasis → STARTED → OUTCOME against Super's own checkout at its own commit, with the real scope digest — the same value check-scope-manifest.sh prints, two paths to one number — admissible? moving true → false across the outcome, five projection surfaces giving five different answers from one ledger, and no host path on any record. Two sessions implemented R7 in parallel and one vocabulary survived. main reached `a43ccfc` with an independent implementation of the same brief (R7/R8/R10 only) — validation-job-started@1 / validation-job-outcome@1, states COMPLETED · FAILED · SOURCE_BASIS_MISMATCH, verdicts HELD · REFUTED, free-form detail, worker_ref as the only subject, no JobBasis. Travis ruled for the underscored vocabulary above, on a narrow ground worth recording: it is GPT's exact ruling including the part a43ccfc departs from — a source-basis mismatch is not a third value beside "it completed" and "it failed", it is the reason a failure has, and promoting one reason to a state makes the enum's members answer two different questions. Merged at 9ecbf25 on branch r0br-r7; their `config.exs` fix came across verbatim (the shared-test-dir defect, which that session measured more carefully and actually repaired while this one only filed it — 11 failures across four files against the shared path, 0 against a private one, same commit, same seed) along with two of their falsifiers, attributed; their test file, whose nineteen cases exercise the retired vocabulary, was removed. Bundle for GPT: ~/Downloads/SUPER_R0BR_R7_VALIDATION_VOCABULARY_FOR_GPT.{md,tar.gz} — GO, 72/72 derived checks held, the generator refusing on any that fail (every failure reason grepped for a producer; no CommandSpec entry reaching job creation while both list_* reads are asserted present; twelve path-shaped field names absent from both record shapes; the dogfood's scope digest required to equal the one check-scope-manifest.sh prints; the host battery required to have measured this host by git diff … -- host/ rather than by commit equality). Two more traps found after the merge: Ampd.Locus.establish/3 registers worktrees in the shared repo and that registration outlives `ampd/priv/data`, so a run after a store reset hits worktree-create-failed on a name git still remembers (the dogfood now prunes and uses a unique name); and committing while an isolated battery runs makes it report CANONICAL TREE MOVED — correctly noting that is not evidence it reached the tree, since it works in ../.super-sabotage-<sha>-<stamp> and is never handed the canonical path. Then GPT returned GO on the vocabulary and REVISE on one producer-boundary hole, and it was right — R0b.R·1 · Typed Receipt Admission closes it. Every R7 invariant held only if a caller CHOSE to enter through Ampd.Validation: Receipts.emit/1 let the caller pick "kind", and Ampd.Validation read validation truth back out of the ledger by kind alone. Reproduced before fixing — Receipts.emit(%{"kind" => "validation_job_started@1", "job_ref" => "vj_fake"}) minted a durable START for a job with no JobBasis, no SourceBasis, no Lane and no Worker, and admissible?/1 then answered true for it; a receipt created executable work, and this round's own suite contained that call (ported from the parallel session, rewritten, passing, and evidence of the defect the whole time). The closure puts the invariants at the store: emit/1 refuses the two validation kinds by name (receipt-kind-requires-typed-admission — refused, not silently re-kinded and not dropped), and they are reachable only through Receipts.record_validation_start/1 and record_validation_outcome/2. Not a flag — no producer field, no internal: true, no process dictionary, no caller-module introspection, since a caller can supply or arrange all of those; the protection is that the protected kinds ride a different message. A ref, never a job — the typed path resolves the JobBasis in its own body, so even Authority.start_validation_job/1, holding the freshly-minted job, passes only job["ref"], and every semantic field on the START is the durable job's while the OUTCOME's subject comes off the START. The relationship checks (a start exists, no outcome yet) moved inside `Ampd.Receipts`' own handler so check and append are one message and cannot interleave; both appends are also @ordered_ops, which is not redundant because ordering is the world's total order across stores and atomicity is this store's log. admissible?/1 gained the JobBasis clause — a ledger row may not create executable work by itself. Four instruments caught the author rather than the code, which is the round's most reusable result: check-ordered-closure.mjs refused an opaque with/else dispatch ("the census cannot follow this dispatch" — removed rather than adjudicated away); the sabotage battery reported NOT A FALSIFIER twice, once because two cases stubbing two different clauses of admissible?/1 both named the same expected test (one test cannot falsify both), once because a stub's substring matched two functions and silently stubbed the one it did not name (an ambiguous stub proves something about a function you did not name); and bash -n caught two broken fragments a staged patch left behind. Final evidence, all at one commit 77eb24b: verify 319/0, ExUnit 683/0, seeds 0 · 424242 · 909090 683/0 each, static gates 8 held, scope vectors 12 held, sabotage-validation 33 caught · 0 NOT A FALSIFIER · 0 unapplied · 0 broke, isolated host sabotage 55 falsified · 0 did not · 0 could not ask with canonical checkout unchanged. The dogfood now carries a negative case — a forged start REFUSED, no ledger append, admissible? false — and its scope digest equals the one check-scope-manifest.sh independently prints. Bundle: ~/Downloads/SUPER_R0BR_R7_R1_TYPED_ADMISSION_FOR_GPT.{md,tar.gz} — GO, 84/84 derived checks. Not done and not claimed: no predicate executes inside a Carrier, no Carrier starts, no terminal input, no SHAPE, no DRIVE; SourceBasis authority is untouched (git diff against the parent shows zero files under host/, cockpit/, dogfood/ or carrier-fixture/).

Last updated: 2026-08-13 — §0 and §6 recomputed against measurement for the first time since April, and three published numbers corrected. The ratings had been carried in the present tense through four months of releases while the header moved; every figure now carries the date it was last actually measured, and §6 has a Verified column so a row cannot silently age again. The recompute moved no percentage — the work since April all landed at live_local or below, and the rows that bound the total (deployed dark-factory pass, adoption) are untouched. Corrections found by measuring: box-and-box is 116 laws with 3 declared-open, not 129 — the cited test/coalition-laws.mjs does not exist, and the suite's own ✓ all 116 stated CC2 compose laws banner overstates its file by 8× (116 is the whole-kernel total hard-coded into the compose suite); the docs atlas serves byte-identical content on 13 hostnames, none redirecting, so ACADEMY.md A1's "the two non-canonical docs hosts" undercounts by ten; and the 1,463-test ecosystem figure has not been re-run since 2026-04-28 and is now labelled historical. Also this session: Alkeyword v0.6.2 inventoried (§2.6, §5) and run end-to-end for the first time, plus Academy added to §5. The tool had shipped a live site, a 22-surface corpus and 15 green witnesses without the loop ever being closed against a real site in one pass. Doing that (opensentience.org: 15 pages, 493 claims, 3 questions × 3 runs on the free WebSearch path) promoted the app from in_tree to live_local and immediately surfaced three defects no unit test could reach — chief among them that brief.py --probe joined probe results by question ID against cluster query text, so the probe stage silently contributed nothing to any brief and the scoring rule that treats a measured citation miss as the strongest available signal was unreachable code. All three fixed, each with a witness watched failing first (18/18). The calibration loop stays in_tree and says so: one baseline now exists, and calibrate.py correctly reports nothing until a published brief sits between two probes. Prior entry: Workbench v0.4.0-alpha — Record: the harness stops asking you to drive an agent and starts recording the one you already drove. Workbench's only path to a bundle was a 563-line in-browser chat page behind a pasted OpenRouter key. That shape is a dead end for subscription auth, because the Claude Agent SDK's OAuth token is licensed for individual use and cannot back a hosted multi-user app — so the surface that uses your subscription has to run locally, and the hosted surface has to stop needing a key. The new `/record` route takes the other road: drop a Claude Code session transcript (~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl) and it becomes a scored SkillBundle — streamed and indexed in the tab, segmented at each user turn, verified against the same six IA-derived gates, redacted on save, into the same library. No model call, no key, nothing uploaded. app/src/lib/ingest/ is pure and browser-safe; app/tools/ingest-transcript.ts (run via the already-present vite-node, no new dependency) is the only thing that reads a real transcript off disk.

Measured against real data, not fixtures. Largest session on this machine: 202 MB / 10,040 records / 75 segments — indexed in 936 ms streaming, largest segment (304 records → 270 edges) built in 1,031 ms → a 21.1 MB bundle. Two passes by design (index retaining nothing, then retain one segment); an ingester that must hold the file to answer "what is in here?" does not survive this corpus. The gates carry signal, and it is checked rather than assumed: every segment is sealed twice, once with each observed capability declared (all six PASS) and once with the most-used capability dropped (gate.no_hidden_capability + gate.authority both FAIL, naming it). An unmapped tool becomes &host.unknown_<name> and never `ambient` — "we don't know what this needs" must stay distinguishable from "this needs nothing".

Three defects in shipped code that only real transcripts surfaced, all pre-existing, all fixed: (1) canonicalize threw on any object with an undefined-valued key, so appendEdge(trace, {kind:'act'}) — a legal edge with no observation — made bundleContentHash throw; now omits such keys per JSON.stringify semantics, which cannot move any existing hash because those inputs used to throw. (2) transcript_pii redaction walked observation only, so a secret handed to a tool (export TOKEN=…, a key written into a config, a bearer token in a URL) survived redaction intact — and the full profile, the one meant for publishing to third parties, kept tool_call.arguments verbatim. Not theoretical: 8 of this project's 25 largest transcripts contain key-shaped strings (one has 260), and a single ingested segment carried 86, four of them in tool arguments → 0 after the fix. (3) applyProfile never redacted the manifest at all, whose name/description/slug derive from the user's own prompt — precisely where a pasted key lands; the slug is now re-derived after redaction, and isIdempotent covers the manifest so gate.redaction_verify covers everything the profile touches.

`checkPhaseOrder` was measuring its own segmentation. It read every tool call in a loop as a learn → act violation — 124 of them on a 124-tool-call segment, every violation on every real segment the same transition. A cycle now also closes when feedback arrives and the next step is not after it, so a faithfully ingested transcript reports 0 violations / 95 cycles where it previously reported 94 violations. The narrowness is deliberate: only a phase at or past learn opens a new cycle, so authorize-after-act is still caught and is pinned by a new test. Two old tests that encoded the previous model were rewritten rather than deleted, with the reason recorded inline.

152 / 152 vitest tests pass (132 through v0.3 + 18 ingest + 2 rewritten phase-order). npm run check is 27 diagnostics, 26 of them pre-existing; the added one is the same "no declaration file for uuid" error four untouched files already carry. Verified live in-browser at /record (streamed index → segment table → crystallize → six gates PASS → save with transcript_pii, then read straight back out of IndexedDB: 0 raw key occurrences, 8 redaction markers, manifest name redacted). Findings, reproduction commands and kill criteria in `workbench/docs/INGEST_SPIKE.md`. Not done, and not claimed: no Claude Code hooks integration, no claude -p driving, no local-app shell, and the OpenRouter path is untouched — the marketing-site / local-app split this points at is a decision, not a delivery.

Last updated: 2026-07-29 — The execution substrate becomes a real layer: WRL / TRVM / WRLM / TRAAVIIS, plus `code` as the orchestration console — and amp-nav v0.8.0 surfaces all five. A month of work in four nested repos that this file had never inventoried. All five are their own GitHub repos, gitignored by ProjectAmp2 per the sub-repo policy; none is deployed, so the honest status for the whole chain is live_local, with the marketing subdomains (trvm.traaviis.com, wrl.traaviis.com, code.traaviis.com) as the only public surfaces.

The chain, in the order a world moves through it — WRLM proposes → WRL seals → TRVM reduces → TRAAVIIS admits. WRLM is the only statistical layer; the other three are total and deterministic. That is the claim the layer is organized around, and it is why they are one nav column rather than four unrelated projects.

  • WallRiderLang (`WRL/`, Core 0.1.2) — an executable topology language whose meaning is a hash. wrl.js is the browser identity spine that seals real sem- ids. Two tracks closed this month: Path B (Semantic IR V2, relation-v2.js — the §D8 Relation Identity Kernel, profile-aware world validation before canonicalization, a required ir 2.0 header, legacy adoption with supplied names) and Path C (unified admission on the source's own ir line; explicit Import V1 as V2 / Adopt these names operations; deriveRuntimeProjection + §D8.18, which makes the V1→V2 downgrade in-band rather than mute; and §D8.19, the projection on the wire — no flags, no prose, only claims a receiver recomputes, so an implementation divergence is refusable rather than silent). 890 conformance checks, 0 failed (node test/conformance.mjs, re-verified this session); register 128 rows, model debt 0. Cross-implementation agreement is real, not asserted: the committed projection vectors round-trip byte-exact through TRVM Forge's independent Python spine, and a shared negative corpus (test/projection-negative-vectors.json) has both verifiers refuse all 15 tampers and agree on the name of every refusal, across two languages and two repos.

  • TRVM (`TRVM/`) — the coordination-free interaction-calculus runtime, and now also the host of Forge. Forge Spinner Bench is at `v0.7.0-alpha.5`, having walked a long ruled slice ladder (v0.4 authoring → v0.5 project/library/persistence → v0.5.1 workspace closure → v0.6 recovery/jobs/startup/migration/perf → v0.6.5.x release + read-only-installation closure → v0.7 template catalog + responsive/a11y closure). Across every one of those slices the pinned demo world still seals to the frozen sem-8ae91fe9…fe4a and every fold stays byte-identical — the discipline is that a packaging or UX slice may not move an identity, and it is checked, not asserted. A separate TRVM/bench/ cross-runtime harness now runs six runtimes on famous math problems: the five IC32-model runtimes give byte-identical normal forms and identical interaction counts; throughput C 34.9M/s > Zig 30.9 > Mojo 15.8 ≫ ic_ref 0.47 > ic_float 0.15, with wasm unranked (V8's call-depth cap ceilings it at 8192 vs ≥2²¹ for the natives). Step 1 is the GoalSpecV1 closed two-sorted AST plus the one adapter; step 2 closes the crossed-source hole (a sealed record can no longer be minted from a result and an artifact that never met) and replaces the flat 768-cell Cartesian product with a derived 320-cell domain — 448 of the published cells had no preimage at all, and marginal coverage structurally cannot see a dead combination. This supersedes the 2026-05-31 §2.4 entry below, which describes the retired v0.1.0 OS-008 harness kernel. Suite status, measured 2026-08-04: 595 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors (~7m38s), up from 532 collected — test/test_mcp.py (M1–M31) and test/test_canonical.py (C1–C30) are new. The K27 defect is closed, and it was not what this file said it was. It was never the linearization: the test fixture wrote the ambient $PATH into the task spec, and since agent_run_policy is inside task- and task_id is an episode-identity key, the host's $PATH moved the episode- id — while never reaching the agent at all, because runner._seal_env (R1) discards caller-supplied PATH. That is why this file recorded episode-0fe5c764…, an earlier handoff recorded episode-7265e90a…, and a third run recorded episode-6a98c47c…: the id was stable within a session and unstable across them, because this box's $PATH carries per-session directories. A second leak had basename(sys.executable) entering trace_id via R4. Production code was correct throughout; the fixtures were contradicting it. The same defect was then found and closed in test_evalone.py and test_ors.py (it did not hold in test_runner.py, which mints only trace-), and the new constant is proven invariant across five simulated hosts. The tests_verifier collection error is gone (renamed at the binding only — the name is in substrate_verifiers.__all__ and wired in wiring.py). `trvs serve --mcp` shipped (MCP revision 2026-07-28, the stateless one — no handshake, no session header; M1–M31, live end-to-end replaying offline to the same reward). A `test_bundle.py::D26` failure not previously recorded was also closed: tools/ has no __init__.py, so import tools.build_packet was resolving to Forge's build_packet.py once engine.py put the Forge checkout on sys.path. Open and escalated, not closed: an RFC 8785 audit (test/test_canonical.py) found the identity canonicalization does not conform to JCS, and the divergence is already realized in a live id — "reward":1.0 vs "reward":1 makes the shipped episode-42d0bb07… an episode-0207bbfc… under JCS. Every receipt hashes a float, so conforming would move essentially every episode- ever minted; that is Travis's call and the current recommendation is to document rather than conform. One free hardening did land (allow_nan=False, proven byte-identical over 73 documents including published dist/ packets, so no id moved). Environment note worth keeping: a first run on this box reported 42 failures, all but two of which were a single environment coupling — trvs resolves python3 to the asdf shim and then runs it under a deliberately scrubbed (hermetic) env, so the shim exits 126 with "No version is set for command python3". Putting a real python3 first on PATH collapses 42 failures to 2. The verifier is behaving correctly; the fixture toolchain resolution is what is host-coupled.

  • `code/` — the `amp` orchestration harness + browser console (own repo c-u-l8er/code, ~20k LOC Python + JS, state in a gitignored .amp/). Workers are Claude Code (claude -p + --resume), each in an isolated amp/<lane> git worktree, budget-capped, and apply refuses to merge. It mints its own worker token by driving claude setup-token over a wide pty (every pty byte goes through redact()), reads worker transcripts straight from ~/.claude/projects/*/<session_id>.jsonl, and now carries a Preview tab that runs what a lane built on its own child port. Two harness-integrity fixes are worth recording because they are the kind that quietly rot a scoreboard: the contradictions gate had no worker and no exit — lane_rungs() takes the maximum rung ever recorded, so a claim recorded at a rung it never earned could never be walked back while still being shown to every proposal in every lane; it now has retract_rung / settle_finding / settle_findings, and a verdict whose consequence the harness cannot itself perform is downgraded to `keep` rather than marked done. And sharpening now stops on measured convergence instead of a flat round cap — which immediately exposed that 12 of 14 sharpen rounds on record had moved the odds down, because the lane's spec was being fed to exploration only and neither review nor sharpen had ever seen it.

amp-nav v0.7.7 → v0.8.0 (ampersand-nav/src/amp-nav.js, synced to 12 sites + 10 extra targets): Code leads Products, TRVM closes Protocols, c-u-l8er.link leads Company, Research gains a fifth column The Execution Substrate and Docs a fourth Execution substrate, and the stale TRAAVIIS tagline ("the harness engineer — OS-008 terminal runtime") is corrected. Two layout fixes came with it: mega-dropdowns are now sized from their own --cols count instead of one shared min-width, and centered on the bar rather than on their trigger — which also fixed a pre-existing bug where the Compose menu ran off the right edge at 1280px. Verified live in a browser (all three placements, and every mega menu fully on-screen).

What this does not claim: none of the five is live_deployed; no third party has driven any of these paths (external); WRLM steps 3–10 are unwritten. The WRL/TRVM/WRLM/TRAAVIIS chain has now been exercised end-to-end as a single pass — TRAAVIIS/tools/end_to_end.py, pins in TRAAVIIS/examples/end-to-end/ — but still not by an outside consumer, which was the other half of that gap and remains open. Two results, and the second is a limit rather than a win: the joins hold (the world's identity derives identically three times — the sem- WRLM carries from capture, Forge's independent lowering of the source, and trvs pack re-lowering from the bytes that landed on disk), and the chain stops at `bundle-`, not `episode-`: a trvm.world.v1 package packs and verifies, then refuses evaluation with SUBSTRATE_NOT_EVALUABLE, because no EpisodeKernelV1 implements TRVM episode semantics (D5 is ruled and unbuilt). That refusal is pinned as an expected outcome, so building the TRVM kernel will fail the pass rather than silently extend it. TRAAVIIS is not installable as advertised — pipx install traaviis 404s, traaviis is an unclaimed PyPI name, and the README said otherwise for months; it now says install-from-source and that is the only path anyone has run. The trvs serve --mcp transport has been driven only by a client written in the same session — no third-party SDK and no Claude Desktop has connected, its pagination is ignored rather than implemented, and it is POSIX-only. The TRAAVIIS K27 identity defect is closed (see §2.6), but the audit that closed the surrounding questions opened a larger one that is not closed: the identity canonicalization does not conform to RFC 8785, and a live shipped `episode-` id already differs.

Last updated: 2026-05-31 (later) — box-and-box v0.9.0 — the evolution surface lands + CC2 coalition schema/lifter ship. Two tracks, both additive, no behavior change to the verdict bridge. Track A — the evolution surface (`evolution.mjs`): the measured/priced/certified self-revision bridge + the provenance substrate box-and-box was missing. Pure, zero-dependency: canon/hash (FNV-1a 32-bit over key-sorted JSON) → digest, a tamper-evident hash-chain (record/chain/verify, GENESIS='00000000'), regresses/delta (non-regression over score vectors), and evolve() — the verdict one level up from govern: govern asks "may this action proceed, and is it best?"; evolve asks "may this policy change (reflexive/entrenchment admissibility), did it measurably improve (axiological non-regression vs. self-declared prediction), is it worth paying for (resource Type-II pricing)?" It checks admissibility first (refuses to weaken an entrenched floor even at large positive Δ), then non-regression, then affordability+worth; on accept it calls revise() and charges the ledger; every verdict ships a certificate {decision∈accept|reject|escalate, predicted, observed, verified, regressed, priced, price, policyBefore/After, rungs:['reflexive','axiological','resource'], record} linked onto the provenance chain. This is the "change manifest pairing every edit with a self-declared prediction verified against outcomes" that Agentic-Harness-Engineering research (arXiv 2604.25850) calls the unsolved self-improvement crux — now the L-E6 non-regression law. 6 new property-tested laws (EV1–EV6) registered in test/laws.mjs (EV1 digest key-order independence, EV2 chain verify+tamper-detect, EV3 refuse-to-weaken-floor, EV4 regressing-change-never-accepted, EV5 priced-accept⇒affordable∧worthwhile∧charged, EV6 certificate soundness); harness now 103 laws (was 97), all passing at 2000 trials each. examples/evolve.mjs extended with a live Ledger demo (accept charged Δ-verified, reject regression, reject weaken-floor). Framed as a join across rungs (reflexive × axiological × resource + provenance), not a ninth rung. Package bumped 0.8.0→0.9.0 (description, ./evolution export, files list); index.mjs re-exports * as evolution; README + bin/arith.mjs + aios/box_and_box_aios.ex 97→103. Track B — CC2 coalition schema + lifter: protocol/schema/v0.1.0/coalition.schema.json (JSON Schema draft 2020-12, the previously-RFC-only CC2 now has a validatable artifact) — required $schema/coalition/version/agents/ensure; clauses map to rungs (agents→alethic join, ensure→strategic ⟨⟨agents⟩⟩◊, common_knowledge→epistemic, owns→deontic, shield→temporal, floor→reflexive, compose→alethic chain+axiological); singleton coalition + empty adversary = the CC1 special case (RFC §6); two examples (ship_it, InfraOperator) validate via ajv. bin/lift.mjs (routed via bin/arith.mjs as box-and-box lift) — the CC1→singleton-coalition lifter: deterministic, no LLM/network, file-or-stdin in → schema-valid coalition on stdout, notes on stderr. Maps agent→name+agents:[self], capabilities[*].need→ensure (else flagged placeholder), governance.hard→floor (un-weakenable by definition), first pipeline steps→compose (op1 |> op2); surfaces escalate_when/soft/autonomy as `compile`'s domain, not structural lift. Verified: lifted infra-operator.ampersand.json validates VALID against the new schema. Pending follow-up: the "97→103" count still needs syncing in website/deploy artifacts (opensentience.org/ living-paper rung pages, site/laws.html, playground.html's "64 of 97" curated subset note, root + AmpersandBoxDesign CLAUDE.md "97 property-tested laws"); and CC2 has a schema+lifter but still no runtime enforcing the coalition admissibility the schema describes (no coalition compose, no joint-trajectory shield check).

RuneFort is now a layout protocol (@runefort/core v0.1.0-alpha.1 Web Components framework, 22 JS files, no SvelteKit); the spec is split across three files at runefort.com/docs/spec/{runefort.protocol.md, runefort.core.md, runefort.dsl.md} totaling 1150 lines (the prior single 1087-line spatial-cognition README is gone, reframed as the supervisor-floor.v1 vocabulary on top of the protocol). Consequence for the shared data layer: BendScript no longer uses Supabase, so the kag.* schema (migrations 010–019) is now orphaned — see §3.1. No deployments changed; ecosystem test count rises from 1,372 to 1,463 (+91, all from BendScript's new protocol-framework test suite).

2026-04-24 — Dark-factory closed loop deployed end-to-end on Fly.io. 10 [&] ecosystem apps live (graphonomous-mcp, os-pulse-mcp, delegatic-mcp, body-browser-mcp, body-os-mcp, prism-eval, fleetprompt, agentelic, specprompt, box-and-box-mcp); three were brand new this session. All three live smoke tests pass against production Graphonomous: fleetprompt crystallization 2/2, PRISM GRASP 3/3, body-browser cross-machine replay 2/2. Same-day fixes: latent Anubis supervision bug in delegatic/body-browser/body-os (HTTP transport had no server registry started); path deps refactored to hex (anubis_mcp) + public git deps (delegatic-engine, opensentience.org) so production Docker builds no longer need multi-project context; body-os-shim + agent-browser CLI bundled into their respective images.

Earlier 2026-04-24 — ALL 7 InstallEngine steps implemented + live FleetPrompt ↔ Graphonomous HTTP roundtrip verified locally. FleetPrompt.InstallEngine now reports 7/7 implemented (step 5 / OpenSentience deploy wired via {:open_sentience, path: "../graphonomous/deps/open_sentience"} — hex publication explicitly off the roadmap, path-dep is the permanent pattern). GraphonomousClient.HTTP gained full MCP session handshake (initialize → notifications/initialized → tools/call with mcp-session-id + SSE-envelope parsing), verified against a real running Graphonomous MCP server locally: initialize_telespace/1 stored a node, retrieve(context) queried it back. Provenance of the figures below (added 2026-08-13). Every bullet in this section and every row in §6 was computed on 2026-04-24/28 and then carried forward in the present tense while the Last updated header moved through four months of releases. Each item is now tagged with the date it was last actually measured. Anything marked (unverified since 2026-04-28) may be true; it has not been checked, and it should not be quoted as current. This file is two documents with different ages (noted 2026-09-19). The dated log above §0 and the increment records below §10 are current — Bend2, the C v2 step, the widened battery, F-X on the resident kind and the Super rounds of 2026-09-18/19 are all in them. The structured sections §0 through §6 are the April and August ledger, and they are the half that answers "where are we". Refreshed mechanically on 2026-09-19: §2.7 added (ten active codebases that had no row, Super among them), §3.4 re-verified against the live hosts, and §2.1–§2.4 and §5 stamped with their row basis. No rating was touched: §0's bullets and §6's percentages are still the April computation, and re-rating them is Travis's exercise, as §6's two flags already say.

  • Overall completion: ~8.3/10 against the full dark-factory vision (April blend; re-examined 2026-08-13 and left unmoved). The composition changed a great deal in four months — Workbench, Alkeyword, Academy, the WRL/TRVM substrate, PARKVPS/T&R, RAVIO — and the blend did not, because every one of those landed at `live_local` or below and the row that bounds the total is adoption/external, which has not moved at all. That is the finding, not an artifact of stale arithmetic: four months of substantial building does not raise this number, and one external consumer would.

  • Protocol layer: ~90% (unverified since 2026-04-28) — 11 OS protocols + 6-primitive [&] algebra; OS-006 has a working authorization kernel with in-memory store; OS-007 still draft; GRASP has two reference impls that pass their conformance suites against deterministic Simulator backends

  • Implementation layer: ~55% (April basis; the denominator has grown since) — 7 shipping-tier products + 4 progressing + 2 frontend apps + 4 spec-only. Not counted in that April basis and shipped since: Workbench v0.4.0-alpha, Alkeyword v0.6.2 (§2.6), Academy (spec + placeholder surface, live), and the TRVM/WRL substrate work. None of them changes the percentage, because none has cleared live_deployed and external.

  • Deployments re-checked 2026-08-13: all 10 Fly.io apps still answer — prism-eval, fleetprompt, specprompt return 200; the MCP servers return 404/405 on / as expected (no root route). `box-and-box-mcp` is still up, which means the "orphaned validator, Fly.io teardown = pending follow-up" note in §3.4 has been pending for three and a half months and is now the oldest open item in this document.

  • Ecosystem test count — last verified 2026-04-28, NOT re-run since: 1,463 tests · 1,463 passing · 0 failures. Four months of commits have landed against these suites without a full-stack re-run, so this is a historical result, not a current guarantee. Re-running it is cheap and nobody has. Net +91 from prior 1,372: BendScript's new protocol-framework test suite reports 96 tests (85 round-trip + 11 harness) replacing the old SvelteKit product's 5. Last full-stack verification before the pivot reconciliation: FleetPrompt grew from 122 to 157 tests (+35) this session — 12 for InstallEngine step 4/6 (Delegatic policy check + Graphonomous connect), 7 for GraphonomousClient.initialize_telespace/1, 9 DB-backed end-to-end install/3 tests, 4 for OpenSentience deploy step 5 (including a real transient-harness start/stop against the live OS-008 runtime), 2 real-HTTP roundtrip tests against a local Bandit fake Graphonomous, and +1 audit_status reorg. All 7 previously-pre-existing failures were real bugs, all fixed: FleetPrompt MCP.Server (2 missing handle_tools_list/0 + handle_tools_call/2 convenience wrappers), Agentelic MCP.Server (1 tools-count drift from 9→10 after agent_ensure was added), PRISM McpClient (4 caused by stdio:// URLs reaching Finch, now short-circuited with typed :stdio_transport_not_supported error that the caller already handles). Three additional latent bugs fixed: all 9 FleetPrompt Ecto schemas used schema "fleet.xxx" with a literal dot (dormant because no test had ever inserted a row — converted to @schema_prefix "fleet"); a manifest unique_constraint whose declared name never matched the real DB constraint; and GraphonomousClient.HTTP lacked MCP session handshake (now does full initialize → notifications/initialized → tool call with mcp-session-id propagation and SSE-envelope parsing, verified against a real running Graphonomous locally).

  • Infrastructure: Shared Supabase (40 migrations, 10 schemas — recounted 2026-08-16) + amp-nav v0.3.3 + 4 Claude Code plugins (unverified since 2026-04-28). Note that §3.1's Supabase route was abandoned by decision after this was written — the products it lists are not all on it.

  • Docs atlas — verified live 2026-08-13: prerendered and deployed, 434 sitemap URLs, canonical + JSON-LD on document pages (spot-checked 150–453 extractable words). But the same deployment answers on 13 hostnames — docs. on agentelic.com, agentromatic.com, ampersandboxdesign.com, bendscript.com, delegatic.com, deliberatic.com, fleetprompt.com, geofleetic.com, graphonomous.com, opensentience.org, specprompt.com, ticktickclock.com and webhost.systems — all returning byte-identical content, all HTTP 200, none redirecting. That is ~5,600 duplicate URLs for 434 documents. ACADEMY.md step A1 says "301 the two non-canonical docs hosts"; the real count is twelve, and the canonical <link> tag every page carries is the only thing currently distinguishing them.

  • Dark-factory closed loop: 7 of 7 steps `live_local`, 0 `in_tree`, 0 missing — the full loop is closed locally. All seven moved in_tree → live_local across the 2026-04-24 session. (The §4 matrix is authoritative here; an earlier "2 of 7" prose read was stale and is corrected throughout this revision. live_local ≠ live_deployed: the loop has been exercised against real local substrates, not yet across deployed cross-machine boundaries — see the next-bar note below.) Step 6 was proved by a cross-BEAM replay test: Process A records a 2-edge trace and stores it in Graphonomous; a fresh mix run BEAM subprocess (Process B) fetches the trace over HTTP, replays against an independently-constructed identical Simulator, and returns status=success, edges_committed=2, edges_attempted=2 at full fidelity. A second test with a deliberately-corrupted state_after confirms the fail-fast invariant (edge 0 committed, edge 1 halts with state_hash_mismatch) crosses the process boundary.

What HASN'T reached `live_deployed` / `external` (the next bars above `live_local`):

  • The dark-factory loop is live_local (real local Graphonomous, real agent-browser CLI + Chromium, real host-exec shim, real cross-BEAM-process replay), but has not been run as a single end-to-end pass across the deployed body-browser-mcp / body-os-mcp / delegatic-mcp Fly.io machines — those machines are up (live_deployed, see §3.4) but no driver has stitched perceive→…→measure across them in one production run.

  • ComputerUse was exercised against a bundled body-os-shim, not against real OpenClaw / Claude Computer Use (external).

  • No competitor memory system (Mem0 / Zep / Letta) has been adapted into PRISM (external).

  • No third-party consumer, benchmark, or contributor has driven any of these paths (external).

Highest-leverage next move: one deployed end-to-end smoke test stitching the already-live_deployed machines into a single production pass — promoting the loop from live_local to live_deployed. The one-command local evidence bundle (scripts/dark_factory_smoke.sh) reproduces the live_local core today; the deployed pass is the remaining bar.

8. Update process

This document is the canonical status reference for the [&] Protocol ecosystem. Every person (or agent) working on the stack should read it before starting non-trivial work and update it on completion of any of these events:

Update triggers

  • A product ships a new version (bump version in §2 tables)

  • A Fly.io/deployment status changes (update §3.4)

  • An OS-0XX protocol advances a stage (draft → spec complete → shipped, update §1.2)

  • A spec crosses 1000 lines or reaches completeness (update §5)

  • A dark-factory step advances a status rung (spec → in_tree → live_local → live_deployed; update §4)

  • A rating component changes materially (update §6)

The status vocabulary (canonical, used stack-wide)

A recurring failure mode in this document has been rating-inflation that conflates "code exists and unit tests pass" with "the pipeline runs end-to-end against real substrates." The 2026-04-24 correction pass walked the overall rating back from a self-assessed 9.2 to 8.3 for exactly this reason. Going forward, every status is one of these five terms — never a bare check / warning / cross glyph:

  • `spec` — specified (and possibly schema'd), but no implementation exists yet.

  • `in_tree` — implemented and unit/property-tested in-tree, but exercised only against stubs / simulators / injected transports / single-process round-trips. Code is present; the system has not been proven against a real external substrate.

  • `live_local` — the code path has been exercised end-to-end against its real substrate at least once on a developer machine (real DB, real browser/CLI, real host, real local server, real cross-process boundary — whichever applies).

  • `live_deployed` — the code path runs in production (e.g. a reachable Fly.io machine) and has been exercised there.

  • `external` — validated by an outside party: a third-party consumer, a published benchmark, an external contributor, or a non-self deployment.

When in doubt, downgrade. Unit tests against an injected transport prove the transform logic is correct (in_tree); they do not prove the system works (live_*). Promote a status only when the named bar is actually cleared.

Update protocol

  1. Edit this file directly. Do not create a sibling status doc.

  2. Update the Last updated date at the top.

  3. Update the specific table(s) affected — keep other rows exact.

  4. If adding/removing a product, update §2.1-§2.4 tables AND §3.1 migrations AND §5 spec completeness.

  5. If the overall rating moves > 0.2, explain in §0 TL;DR's "What's different from 6 months ago" line.

  6. Do not fabricate counts or statuses. When uncertain, use ? or note "status unknown".

  7. For adoption metrics (§6 adoption row), only count verifiable external usage (published benchmarks, external contributors, third-party deployments).

What this document is NOT

  • A product roadmap — that lives in individual spec docs

  • A marketing artifact — write honestly, including what's missing

  • A protocol reference — SPEC.md, PROTOCOL_PROMPT.md, and OS-00X docs are authoritative

  • A CHANGELOG — per-project CHANGELOG.md files track their own history

What this document IS

  • The authoritative answer to "where are we on stack completion right now?"

  • A quick reference for any agent (human or AI) joining the work

  • A sanity check against marketing copy (index.html should not claim more than this doc)

9. Appendix: terminology

  • Shipped — published to npm/hex/pypi OR deployed to production hosting OR both

  • Progressing — substantial source code (≥40 non-boilerplate files) + passing tests + deployment config present

  • Spec complete — authoritative spec ≥ 400 lines, normatively structured, approved for implementation

  • Draft — spec exists but incomplete or superseded

  • OS-0XX — OpenSentience protocol number (OS-001 through OS-011 currently)

  • [&] — the composition protocol (AmpersandBoxDesign)

  • PULSE — OS-010 temporal loop manifest standard

  • PRISM — OS-009 benchmark engine (Rating Iterative System Memory)

  • Dark factory — machine-hosted agents operating autonomously with continual learning and cross-machine skill transfer

  • InteractionTrace — GRASP canonical record of a perception-action cycle (defined in opensentience.org/docs/spec/OS-011-EMBODIMENT.md)

  • SurpriseSignal — PULSE v0.1.1 canonical token emitted when an actual observation diverges from a forward-model prediction; consumed by novelty detection, PRISM calibration scoring

  • MCP — Model Context Protocol (Anthropic); the runtime transport that &memory/&reason/&body/etc. capabilities compile to

  • A2A — Agent-to-Agent protocol (Google); the coordination transport that a2a_skills on [&] contracts compile to

  • BYOR — Bring Your Own Repo; PRISM feature that lets you benchmark a memory system against your actual codebase

  • FSM — Finite State Machine; implicit structure formed by the set of {StateHash, TypedAction, StateHash} triples across recorded InteractionTraces

  • hex.pm — the Elixir package registry (some protocols are hex-published, some still vendored)

  • amp-nav — the shared navigation Web Component distributed to every portfolio marketing site (v0.3.3 current)

10. How to verify this document

To audit this document's claims, run:

# From ProjectAmp2 root
cd graphonomous && mix test 2>&1 | tail -3                  # Graphonomous test count
cd ../PULSE && npm test 2>&1 | tail -5                       # PULSE conformance
cd ../PRISM && mix test 2>&1 | tail -3                       # PRISM test count
cd ../AmpersandBoxDesign/reference/elixir/ampersand_core && mix test 2>&1 | tail -3  # [&] reference
cd /home/travis/ProjectAmp2/specprompt.com && mix test 2>&1 | tail -3   # SpecPrompt
cd ../agentelic.com && mix test 2>&1 | tail -3              # Agentelic
cd ../fleetprompt.com && mix test 2>&1 | tail -3            # FleetPrompt
cd ../WebHost.Systems/apps/web && npm test 2>&1 | tail -5   # WebHost.Systems (if present)
cd ../bendscript.com && npm test 2>&1 | tail -5             # BendScript (post-pivot: 96 tests via vitest)

# Check Fly.io deployment configs exist
find . -name fly.toml -not -path '*/node_modules/*' -not -path '*/deps/*'

# Check shared Supabase migrations
ls ampersand-supabase/migrations/ | wc -l

# Check amp-nav version
grep -o 'amp-nav v[0-9.]*' ampersand-nav/*.md | head -1

# Spec line counts
for dir in */docs/spec; do
  echo "$dir: $(wc -l < $dir/README.md 2>/dev/null) lines"
done | sort -t: -k2 -n -r

If any output disagrees with a claim in this doc, update the doc (not the other way around) — ground truth comes from the running systems.

This file is version-controlled. The most recent authoritative version is always at `/home/travis/ProjectAmp2/STACK_COMPLETION.md` on the `main` branch.

Road shell (Tier 1) — 2026-09-10 — SPECIFIED; PROOF BUILT AND GREEN ON LINUX, PRODUCT NOT IMPLEMENTED

Status: the spec is a `spec`-rung proposal with 6 open [TRAVIS] decisions. The only code that exists is a standalone falsification harness (`RRABBIT/tier1-proof/`). No product, no road, no integration with `super/cockpit`. Discoverability does not imply approval.

Travis ruled Tier 1 only — an app standing on a T&R road is a webview; streamed native windows stay compositor-proxy's job and other applications' macOS windows are out of scope. Spec at RRABBIT/docs/ROAD_SHELL.md (spec rung, 7 open [TRAVIS] decisions in §13).

The design is assembled from primitives that already exist and are cited in place: super/cockpit/Cargo.toml:17 already enables Tauri's unstable multi-webview feature and super/cockpit/src/preview.rs:138 already opens an external URL in a child webview at an arbitrary rect with a navigation policy; RRABBIT/m2/world.js slotAt/slotFree/ nextFreeSlot is the placement allocator; RRABBIT/m2/ops.js apply(op) is the seam, which a road shell would make its fourth consumer and the first whose actor is another program. The proposal adds one tier — live, a real child webview — above hidden/card/paint, and resolves the one architectural collision (an OS webview is an axis-aligned rectangle and cannot be drawn into the three.js scene) with the pose that already exists: live only in the read pose, an app-published representation everywhere else.

Reviewed the same day; five corrections applied and recorded in DOCTRINE rather than silently: pose eligibility is not a resource budget (cast already pins a tier past its pose, so the live budget is a separate rule, N = 1 for v1); declared capability / reported availability with an expiry / coordinator acceptance are three facts and only the third may show work as transferred; a webviews:-scoped capability gates invoke and not what happens at apply(op), where authorization must key on an authenticated principal that is not the caller-supplied by; Channel::send returns Result<()> and the accurate claim is that a successful send does not establish receipt or processing (WebviewEvent is #[non_exhaustive] — one variant in 2.11.5, not one forever); and "macOS is easier" is a hypothesis with a six-row test list, with dataStoreIdentifier corrected to macOS 14+/iOS 17+ website-data separation rather than per-pane security isolation.

Next is one narrow proof and nothing else (§12): published sign → read pose → live pane → leave read pose → published sign, with state preserved and stale messages rejected — nine assertions, four sabotages, built in its own harness so that re-rooting the cockpit does not answer §13 #1 by accident. Nothing is measured yet; no number in the spec is a claim about this scene's cost. See RRABBIT/docs/ROAD_SHELL.md.

Ruled the same day (§13 #5, so 7 open decisions became 6): the principal is a host-owned identity for a specific pane binding, with explicitly assigned grants, derived by the host from the invoking webview and its current binding generation; the page can supply neither. by stays an untrusted log annotation, a label identifies a surface and confers nothing, revoking a binding rejects its delayed operations, and a recorded identity carries no authority. The consequence that reshaped the build is §6.2.1: `ops.js` is page JavaScript, so a page-side `apply` cannot enforce any of this — the vocabulary seam (page) and the authority check (host) are two things, and every privileged effect passes through the second.

`RRABBIT/tier1-proof/` — built and green, 2026-09-10. published sign → read pose → live pane → leave read pose → published sign, with state preserved and stale messages rejected: 23 held · 0 failed on the live battery (real WebDriver clicks and keys), 10 held · 0 failed on the static ACL gate, and all four sabotages are falsifiers — each reddens exactly the assertions it should. Confirmed by the compiler that tauri::Webview is injectable as a command argument, which is what makes the principal host-derived rather than asserted. capabilities/road.json over-grants allow-privileged-intent to the road on purpose so that what refuses it is the seam and not tauri's resolver, and an assertion checks that distinction.

Three findings kept. A Tauri CSP naming `connect-src` for IPC blocks the app from fetching its own manifest (connect-src ipc: … excludes 'self'; fetch throws Load failed and the symptom is a page that never becomes ready with an empty console) — and since §5 makes every CD app's sign a fetched manifest, that is the road shell's trap, not the harness's. The battery was not idempotent — /value appends and localStorage outlives the app — and it was the sabotage sweep that exposed it, by reddening two assertions the sabotages do not touch. Restoring source is not restoring the artifact: the sweep left the sabotaged binary in target/release and the next run measured it, the same class as the baked-UI trap.

Not measured: the read pose on screen (the GtkBox positioning defect is not worked around in the harness), an actual renderer crash (only controlled teardown), source unavailability (there is no dev server), and anything at all on macOS. See RRABBIT/docs/ROAD_SHELL.md §12 and RRABBIT/tier1-proof/README.md.

Revised later the same day, after review. The first report called the harness green while the read pose was failing, and that was the wrong shape: geometry is half the central promise — a road that collapses to one pixel when a pane goes live has not performed the transition, whatever the authority assertions say. The read pose is an acceptance gate now, and the standalone probe remains only as the platform instrument and the macOS contract. Three design tightenings landed with it: the principal is resolved from the injected Webview through the host-owned binding registry (authorize takes &tauri::Webview, never a label string — which made one sabotage uncompilable); manifest discovery moved to the coordinator, with the CSP's connect-src back to ipc: only and a static assertion that the road page contains no `fetch` at all; and identity is pulled, not pushed, after eval-injecting the generation at startup raced the page's first script.

Now: 25 held · 0 failed live, 15 held · 0 failed static, all FIVE sabotages falsifiers. §10.6 is CLOSED on Linux — road 1000 × 653, pane 522 × 262 at the requested rect — via a GtkOverlay port that needed two GTK facts the cockpit's version does not: set_size_request is a minimum a WebKitWebView's natural size exceeds (685 × 560), and margins are subtracted a second time inside the allocation returned from get-child-position (207 × 169 = 522−315 by 262−93). The read pose is reached asynchronously, ~2.8 s here, full-window at first paint — so a road drawing its own chrome will see that frame, and a geometry assertion made before layout settles is not one: measured early, the road check passed under the sabotage that removes the layout call.

Four instrument findings kept. An accidental edit injected two sabotages at once; the static gate caught the authority one before any test ran and nothing static could catch the skipped layout call — only the live geometry gate did, which is the argument for the promotion, made by accident. A str.replace that matches nothing still prints success: two edits reported themselves done and changed nothing, one of which was then stated as fact, and the static gate rather than any reading is what caught it. The sabotage sweep called a red battery green whenever its grep drifted, on two sabotages that had reddened it — it reports three outcomes now. And restoring source is not restoring the artifact.

Still not measured: an actual renderer crash (only controlled teardown), source unavailability (there is no dev server), and anything at all on macOS — tier1-proof/tools/geometry-probe.mjs is that contract in one command: parent 1000 × 653, child 522 × 262.

Reviewed again the same day; two load-bearing issues closed and one gate narrowed. Now: 28 held · 0 failed live, 18 held · 0 failed static, 4 registry unit tests, seven sabotages. RRABBIT/tier1-proof/.

Eventual geometry is not containment. The ~2.8 s asynchronous read pose was reported as a timing note and it was a containment defect: an untrusted pane covered the entire road and took input over all of it for that whole window, while every post-settle assertion passed. A pane is now neither visible nor interactive until its allocation is the read pose and then becomes both at once — opacity 0 plus insensitive, not hidden, because a GTK widget that has never been shown is never laid out. A pose that never arrives abandons the promote. Measured: 73 samples from creation through settling, none visible or interactive outside the rectangle, 2709 ms contained, and 7 ms to settle after reveal because by then it is already correct.

`whoami` was the hole in generation invalidation. It takes no echoed generation — it is what a caller uses to learn one — so under a reusable label an instance that outlived its close() could resolve the name to whichever binding now held it and come back carrying the successor's generation. A pane's label is now its instance (pane-<generation>, never reused), its capability is minted per instance at runtime via CapabilityBuilder (a static capability file cannot express this, since it names a fixed label), revocation precedes destruction, and the registry's unit tests assert the refusal deterministically — a renderer that survives its own close cannot be summoned on demand, so the live battery asserts the structure and the registry asserts the behaviour. One unit test demonstrates the leak itself on a still-reusable label.

A synchronous `#[tauri::command]` runs on the main thread, so a command that waits for the platform blocks the work it is waiting for: the overlay sat at GTK's never-allocated sentinel for the full deadline while place and allocation both succeeded (with_webview runs inline when already on the main thread). Every instrument answered and only the layout never happened. Any host-side wait must be async.

One gate narrowed rather than kept. Banning fetch from the road outright was broader than the architecture and would have been retired the first time a road needed unrelated network access, taking the real assertion with it. What is asserted now is the durable law: manifest discovery goes through the host-owned package path and cannot silently fall back to a page fetch.

macOS is an explicitly unverified target and its runtime check is a release gate, not a development blocker. CI compiles and unit-tests on macos-14 and prints on every run that it validated no geometry, no containment and no input; tier1-proof/tools/geometry-probe.mjs is the real gate in one command, portable to a borrowed or hosted Apple Silicon Mac. The pane's on-screen position, previously named as unverified, is now MEASURED from outside the process: 1044x524+630+186 against an expected 1044 × 524 at (630, 186), delta 0 on all four (tier1-proof/tools/pose-screenshot.mjs; pictures at RRABBIT/docs/tier1-read-pose.png and -probe.png). A two-capture difference is not the measurement — clicking read also hides the sign and rewrites the status block, so the changed region came back 1915x1386; the pane has to identify itself by painting a colour that appears nowhere else. The capture goes through XWayland (GDK_BACKEND=x11) because this box is GNOME/Wayland with no grim, so the layout measured is backend-independent but the capture path is not the shipping one, and the probe needs a display and ImageMagick so it is a bench instrument rather than a gate. An actual renderer death is now measured too (tier1-proof/tools/renderer-crash.mjs, 12 held · 0 failed): SIGKILL to the pane's own WebKitWebProcess — each webview gets one, so the road's is untouched and a pane crash does not take the shell down. §10.1 holds exactly as written: unresponsive and never gone while the dead pane is left alone (a clock cannot pronounce death), present true throughout because tauri emits no destroyed event, WebKitGTK does not respawn it, and demote-then-promote recovers into a new instance. Two things the probe had to be built around: a renderer crash deletes the WebDriver session, so the road records the timeline to its own storage and drives its own recovery; and both of the probe's own bugs were assertion WINDOWS — counting the demote's correct gone as a violation, and reading the renderer count where the replacement looks like a revival. Source unavailability is blocked on a ruling rather than on effort: the harness bakes its UI into the binary, so there is no origin to take away, and reaching the condition needs a pane on an external origin — which is ROAD_SHELL.md §13 #7, still unruled. Building it would answer that decision by accident, which is the reason the harness is standalone at all.

One entry point, with a receipt. tier1-proof/tools/verify.mjs runs every instrument — build, registry unit tests, static ACL gate, live battery, geometry contract, renderer death, on-screen position, and (with --sweep) the sabotage sweep — and writes receipts/VERIFY-<stamp>.md carrying the commit, the host's capabilities and every count. It states what it skipped and why, and refuses to say "all held" when anything was skipped. Its own first version is the reason that matters: it probed for tools with --version, which tauri-driver does not answer, skipped every stage that mattered, and reported all stages held · 5 skipped. A capability probe that errs toward SKIP is the worst kind — the run goes green having tested nothing.

Road shell (Tier 1) — 2026-09-11 — the second proof: two apps across one boundary

RRABBIT/tier1-proof/tools/handoff-battery.mjs, 21 held · 0 failed on its first run. The first proof answered whether a pane can stand on a road; this asks whether the rules compose across an app boundary, which is where they can first contradict each other. Two packages in the coordinator's catalogue — notes (accepts document, produces summary) and digest (accepts summary, produces nothing).

Established: both signs render with zero live panes (§5's claim in its strongest form — nothing started in order to lay out a road); routing reads the declaration, with an unroutable kind refused NO_ROUTE by name rather than dropped; an app's report is not a transfer — the ledger stays empty while the app works and the road has nothing to route until the coordinator accepts, and what the app gets back is the coordinator's record; eviction is how the second app stands, not an optimisation; authority does not cross the boundary — digest is never granted offer and the host refuses it; each app's state survives its own eviction; package-prefixed keys prevent collisions but the shared origin does not prevent cross-app reads (corrected 2026-09-12). There is at most one live pane at every observation.

`N > 1` was not needed for any of it, and assuming otherwise would have blocked this behind §13 #6: the budget limits simultaneous live panes. The piece worth keeping is a grant derived from a declaration — grants_for reads the manifest's produces and grants offer only where something is produced, the instance capability mirroring it, so what an app may do is a consequence of what it said it was. That refusal is defended at three layers and the sabotage falsifying it must dismantle all three.

The sweep is ten sabotages now. Receipts became build artifacts: one committed alongside the revision it describes was written before that revision existed and permanently recorded working tree dirty, so receipts/ is git-ignored, CI uploads them, and a receipt names the tested revision and says loudly when the tree was not clean. Still open: macOS, and source unavailability (blocked on §13 #7).

Super — 2026-09-11: five days of application work committed, and the companion carries the consent queue

The tree was consolidated. super/ had 197 untracked files, 21,815 lines plus 3,123 tracked additions sitting five days past its last commit (1671d82, 2026-09-06) — the whole application layer, the three new ampd modules, the mobile gateway and the harness. It is now four layered commits, each verified as found and none rewritten: bbe1a09 the 49 round documents · 4f62a61 ampd (bot identity, development tasks, development attempts) · eac24f8 the mobile gateway · 2fc6bdc the application layer. Green at the point of commit: static gates 8 held · 0 failed · 0 could not run, ampd ExUnit 753 · 0 (baseline at 77eb24b was 683 · 0), mobile gateway 11 · 0, intent surface 6 held covering 25/25 mutations, webview ACL 35 held over 27 commands. The heavy WebKitWebDriver suites were not rerun and are not claimed; their results live in the round documents at the commits they were taken against.

Why the application layer is one commit rather than a feature series. Every feature in it is registered in the same three files — cockpit/build.rs's command list, main.rs's module set and invoke handler, and capabilities/default.json. Splitting by feature means splitting hunks in those three, and every intermediate commit would either fail to compile or fail check-webview-acl.mjs, which holds exactly when the commands the host declares are the commands the page invokes. A commit that cannot be checked is not a smaller unit of review.

Then: the two collections that mean "a person is being asked" were the two not on the wire. The mobile companion published seven projection collections and none was grant_requests or pending_approvals — the runtime stopped, waiting on a person, which is the desktop's own first two sections. The visible symptom was Needs me printing "Nothing is waiting on a decision" with no basis for it; on Travis's own host, which has zero development tasks, that was the only sentence the screen could produce while a held effect would have been invisible.

Both queues are published now (9825e31, app cfebefb), narrowed to a named set of fields — the one place in mobile_gateway.rs where the allowlist is over fields rather than collections, because a pending approval carries the request envelope and the caller's whole held context. A Rust test puts a credential in held_ctx and a command line in envelope and asserts neither appears anywhere in the serialised snapshot. The phone still cannot answer: 405 is unchanged and the cards say where consent is given.

[] and null are kept apart everywhere — empty means nobody is asking you, null means this app does not know; the count draws -- rather than 00 and a card names the queue the host did not publish. Evidence: cargo test mobile_gateway 6 · 0 (4 new), gateway 11 · 0, gates 8 held, app npm test 39 · 0 and tsc clean, rendered on the Android emulator against the real connector and gateway in both the populated and --damaged cases.

The open decision this creates, stated and not ruled: NIST SP 800-53 IA-2(13) treats confirming a privileged action on a second device as a strengthening — the requesting and confirming channels are independent, which a bot inside the runtime and a phone on a separate transport genuinely are. But "what you see is what you sign" cuts the other way, and the narrowing above means a phone cannot sign what it cannot see. Consent to a hash it cannot read, send the envelope, approve a class instead of an instance, or keep the phone as a nudge — that is the decision, and it is an authority question across gateway, connector, cockpit and ampd rather than a UI one. Push, separately, is impossible without Apple or Google: the honest form is a content-free wake with the content fetched over the private path.

Super dogfood cycle 1 — 2026-09-12: the first change set Super holds about itself, and the two ceilings it cannot carry

tools/dogfood-setup.mjs --real ran against Travis's own world for the first time and opened its lane against the wrong repository. Two were registered and the projection published %{"ref" => ref} for both, discarding the stored record that holds the path, so the setup's ?? repos[0] had no rule available but "the first one" — and took ProjectAmp2/computedriven.com for work on ProjectAmp2/super. The lane form named them Repository 1 and Repository 2: not the reference, but an ordinal references.js invents for a record with no name, i.e. two source trees told apart by the order they happened to be registered in. Nothing undoes this. There is no close_lane, and delete_workspace refuses a workspace that holds one by design ("Lanes retain their ancestry"). Recovery was to re-create the five plans on a correct lane and cancel the originals with a note naming the cause (tools/dogfood-recover-lane.mjs, new this round, plans first so a refusal strands nothing); wk_0017 closed, ln_0016 left on record because nothing can remove it. The setup no longer guesses: --repo=<ref>, or a name match, or it stops — and its lane and plan idempotence keys are (goal, actor, repository) and (lane, title, not cancelled), because matching a lane on the actor alone is what made a lane on a different repository read as this one already being set up.

Proposal 2 revised to Travis's ruling — the name is shown alongside the reference, never replacing it, because two path segments can still collide. The rule went into the one function that decides how a record is displayed (references.js): a repository's label is name · ref, and ref alone when no name is published. Three things had to follow it. record-page.js was re-resolving an already-resolved label, printing the name twice (readable is deliberately not idempotent). And the lane form's control was 290px too narrow — it rendered ProjectAmp2/computedriven.com · rp_ and cut off exactly the half that disambiguates, which would have satisfied the letter of the change and none of its point; 290px is measured (246px of text at 12px system-ui + 18px padding + 22px arrow), not chosen. Before/after taken live from the page's own DOM on the same world: ["Repository 1","Repository 2"] → ["ProjectAmp2/computedriven.com · rp_0001","ProjectAmp2/super · rp_0002"]. Evidence: ampd 777 · 0 (was 771), reference-label-test.mjs 7 · 0 and falsified — 6 of the 7 fail against the unchanged source, the seventh is the control that must pass either way, twelve further JS suites 65 · 0, gates 8 held. cockpit/ui/bots.js:128 still re-narrows repositories to {ref} before provider context and nothing here relaxes it.

Proposal 1 is recorded in the world: `da_0030`, `development-review-set@1`, status `recorded`, provenance `human-recorded-review-material` — three files, submitted through record_development_change_set, the same intent door every form uses, with the runtime recomputing every digest, unsaved, and whole-set coherence. Nothing is accepted and nothing is applied. The tree is reverted and the release rebuilt to d3a7acc4465a607350a7f2f737a6bf044d038f7945ad6c3b437f1d0669187ee1 — byte-identical to the build this round started from, which is what proves the revert complete; sha256sum /proc/<pid>/exe on the running desktop reports the same hash.

Proposal 2 cannot be submitted at all, and that is the round's finding. Two independent ceilings, both measured rather than read: seven files were refused by the bridge — frame of 336202 bytes exceeds the 262144 byte limit — before the validator saw them; and a two-file subset, a legal count, was refused attempt-fields-invalid. A change set carries whole file text, not a diff, under shared_draft ≤ 24000 and proposed_text ≤ 32000 per file, so Super cannot review a change to its own projection (34,282 B), its own UI entry point (72,809 B) or its own stylesheet (35,044 B). No subset was submitted: without projection.ex nothing publishes a name and the rest do nothing, so a subset would be an incomplete proposal wearing a complete one's record. Second finding from the same probe: the byte refusal reads "A change set needs two to four complete, valid file replacements" — the count was two. set_file?/1 folds membership, byte caps, text validity and every digest into one boolean, so every failure returns the sentence about counting. Both are now plans in the world (dt_0031, dt_0032), alongside the five recovered ones.

Desktop relaunched after Travis's reboot as super-desktop with the companion (mobile/start-local.sh, SUPER_MOBILE_PANEL=1): unit active, world lock held, ampd BEAM up (a green port is not a green host), gateway 127.0.0.1:4318. A systemd user unit inherits neither asdf nor nvm and host/src/lib.rs:1823 is Command::new("mix"), so PATH and LANG are set on the unit explicitly. Private tailnet and connector restarted — super-mobile and iphone-12-mini both on the tailnet, serve config intact, and the chain probes 401 / 401 / 403 / 403 / 405 / 401 tlsVerified:true exactly as documented. super-mobile-observer deliberately left down: it would contend for the world lock the desktop holds and park, which looks like success.

Driven on a real screen with a local provider fixture, since the decode and the guard run on every reply whatever the provider (tools/first-reply-title-only-smoke.mjs, 16 held · 0 failed from both trees, the installed binary included): the measured shape lands nothing, keeps the parsed title, restores the draft, and the resend does not ask for a title again — proven from the fixture's own record of the second request; the same unterminated header carrying a proposal is not refused, so the guard is about emptiness, not the header. The cause is now MEASURED (2db9d36, binary e4882fd0… installed 2026-09-19 01:05Z): once Travis restored the CLI sign-in, the byte-faithful runner reproduced it on the first try — the model's first StructuredOutput call was 92 bytes carrying only {"text":"<conversation-title>…"} with no `actions`, the CLI refused it against the schema, and its second call was the complete 2 832-byte answer plus a 13 693-byte propose_file_edit. What decided the 09-18 outcome was actions: bots.rs requires an array, so the call that reached the page carried actions: [] — schema-valid, nothing to retry. No schema can say "the text must be more than its own header", so the page-side guard is the fix, not a workaround. One of two title-requesting runs was premature and the control was the only run that wrote a prose block at all: a reproduction and a hint, not rates. The stream exposed a second defect, fixed here: ReplyState.partial is one raw-JSON accumulator and nothing reset it between tool calls, so after a refused call the live view parsed the FIRST, abandoned object and sat on the 79-character header — and on "79 bytes received" — for the whole retry; observe_reply now clears it on a new tool_use block, pinned by a test that fails with the stale header when the clear is disabled. cargo test --bin super-cockpit 105 passed · 1 ignored; smokes against the installed binary 16/16, 13/13, 9/9.
